A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. All appendix pages have identical text and rendered content, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on MNIST variants, molecular datasets, RxRx3, and proprietary phenomics data, plus empirical calibration and stopping-criterion analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, including acquisition-performance curves and repeated-trial stopping results.

M1.justification: The inference-set-design procedure, confidence-based acquisition, stopping criterion, and predictor remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the regression adaptation in Appendix E.1 are identical.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same MNIST variants, QM9 classification, Molecules3D regression, and RxRx3 and proprietary phenomics tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods, including random sampling, BALD, diversity sampling, and heuristic orderings where previously evaluated. The newly cited transductive methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, acquisition batches, metrics, training settings, and stopping thresholds are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C–F, including Table 2.

E4.justification: MNIST corruption sensitivity, difficult-example acquisition, chemical-element coverage, weak-calibration checks, and stopping-criterion validation are retained without revision, including Figures 3, 4, 6, 10, 12, and 13.

E5.justification: Both retain three-seed averages, standard-error shading, and stopping-time minimum–maximum intervals. Appendix F.2 still reports 100 seeds for MNIST variants and QM9 and 50 seeds for phenomics.

E6.justification: The plotted results and reported findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 5 retains QM9 savings of 53.6% for LC, 53.8% for BALD, and 16.6% for random acquisition.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, weak-calibration assumption, Lemma 1, stopping bound, and Appendix A proofs and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: inference set design, confidence-based acquisition, a probabilistic stopping criterion, and experimental cost reductions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of acquisition gains and limited RxRx3 benefits are unchanged. Both retain the limitation that observed labels are assumed deterministic and perfectly accurate, despite noise in biological experiments.

D1.justification: Dataset processing, implementation details, hyperparameters, and code-access information are unchanged. Both retain the same disclosure that the Figure 8 dataset is proprietary.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds transductive experimental design as related work, citing Yu et al. (2006) and Hübotter et al. (2024). It extends the discussion of held-out evaluation and restricted acquisition budgets to this research line; other positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The related-work paragraph receives a short explanatory addition and local wording edits. The remaining narrative and section order are preserved; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 7, with accompanying shifts in text and figure placement and reference pagination. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves scholarly context by explicitly connecting the work to transductive experimental design and adding two relevant references in Section 3. The scientific methods, evidence, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to more complete research positioning.
